Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag has claimed Cristiano Ronaldo let the team and him down during their time together at Old Trafford. In an exclusive interview with The Athletic on Tuesday, Ten Hag said: “He let the team down, and he let me down, because we planned with him. I flew out to Portugal to speak with him about what I was aiming for before I came to United. ”Obviously, he’s one of the best in football history. I respected him a lot. But at that time, as a manager, I had to make a rational decision.” Ten Hag alleged that Ronaldo struggled with fitness and preparation. He claimed the forward pulled out of training sessions, failed to reach required heart-rate levels, and completed only two of three laps in a running punishment after United’s 4-0 defeat at Brentford in August 2022. “I confronted him with this,” Ten Hag said. “Many times I say, ‘Ronnie, everyone wants to work for you to bring you in the right position, but if you can’t bring yourself in the box, you can’t score’. He was not capable to do this.” Iwobi backs Fulham resurgence after first EPL win EPL: Maddison inspires Spurs to first league win of season Portugal FA hands Ronaldo 30-day suspension, €255 fine He added that Ronaldo “ran neither in possession nor out of possession” because “he didn’t prepare himself” and told teammates to “save your legs at the training.” “Ronaldo was telling the players: save your legs at training”. “I understand it when you are top fit, but first you have to train yourself to get into the right fitness levels” “Every top team has to embrace the top player, but the top player has to work for the team,” Ten Hag said.
